title: Handle Engram's control_request_expired as certified non-application: keep the checkpoint report, auto-retry admission with the same key
outcome: When Engram returns control_request_expired on any control verb, TermAl treats it as a certified no-effect result: it keeps retained reports and intents and retries with the same idempotency key. It never loses turn evidence and never strands a queue on that code.
acceptance: A closing checkpoint that receives control_request_expired keeps the turn report, so the next closing attempt carries the same report. A regression proves the report, including a host-recorded test run, survives one expired attempt and is delivered on the retry.
An admission evaluate that receives control_request_expired enters the automatic retry schedule with the same idempotency key, not a Reconcile hold. A regression covers this.

Begin and end responses with control_request_expired are classified as certified non-application for that invocation, and are retried or reconciled with the same key. Regressions cover both. The code is never synthesized from a host-side timeout: a local deadline still yields deadline_exceeded with unknown outcome.
